Qatar Tourism Sector Faces Severe Credit Freeze Amidst Plunging Bookings

A deepening credit freeze has sent shockwaves through Qatar’s tourism industry, with firms reporting acute liquidity shortages and a sharp fall in bookings as the crisis unfolds. The Qatar Tourism Business Association (QTBA) this week reported that over 75% of its member companies are struggling to access short-term financing, with banks tightening lending criteria and declining new loan applications since late March.

“The abrupt halt in credit availability has left many operators unable to cover routine expenses, let alone invest in new offerings,” said Hassan Al-Mansoori, Chair of the QTBA. “Unless immediate measures are taken, we risk widespread closures.” Industry sources indicate that several prominent tour operators, including Desert Gateway Tours and Pearl City Experiences, have suspended new reservations, citing uncertainty over their ability to fulfill upcoming bookings.

Popular heritage sites, such as the Al Zubarah Fort and Souq Waqif, have seen a significant drop in visitor numbers over the past month, as travel agencies scale back promotions and guided tours. According to the Qatar Tourism Workers Union, hundreds of guides, hospitality staff, and event coordinators have been placed on unpaid leave as firms grapple with cash shortages. 

“Staff are anxious about the future,” said union spokesperson Fatima Rahman. “Many workers depend on these jobs, and the impact is growing each week.” 

Industry analysts warn that, with no immediate signs of relief in credit markets, the crisis could persist well into the peak travel season. The Ministry of Tourism has convened an emergency task force but has yet to announce concrete support measures.
